## externaldns.k8s.io/v1alpha1

### DNSEndpoint

DNSEndpoint declares DNS records for external-dns to publish.

    <tr><th>Name</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th><th>Required</th></tr>

#### DNSEndpoint.spec

[↩ Parent](#dnsendpoint)

DNSEndpointSpec defines the desired state of DNSEndpoint

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Name</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th><th>Required</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><b><a href="#dnsendpointspecendpointsindex">endpoints</a></b></td>
      <td>[]object</td>
      <td>
        Endpoints is the list of DNS records this resource declares.
        <br/><i>Item validation</i>: <code>self.recordType != &#39;SRV&#39; || !has(self.targets) || self.targets.all(t, t.endsWith(&#39;.&#39;))</code>
        <br/><i>Message</i>: SRV targets must be &#39;&lt;priority&gt; &lt;weight&gt; &lt;port&gt; &lt;host&gt;&#39; with an absolute host, e.g. &#39;10 5 5060 sip.example.com.&#39;
        <br/><i>Item validation</i>: <code>self.recordType != &#39;NAPTR&#39; || !has(self.targets) || self.targets.all(t, t.endsWith(&#39;.&#39;))</code>
        <br/><i>Message</i>: NAPTR targets must be absolute and end with a dot
        <br/><i>Item validation</i>: <code>self.recordType != &#39;PTR&#39; || self.dnsName.lowerAscii().endsWith(&#39;.in-addr.arpa&#39;) || self.dnsName.lowerAscii().endsWith(&#39;.ip6.arpa&#39;)</code>
        <br/><i>Message</i>: PTR dnsName must be a reverse DNS name under .in-addr.arpa or .ip6.arpa, written without a trailing dot, e.g. &#39;1.0.0.10.in-addr.arpa&#39;
        <br/><i>Max items</i>: 1000
      </td>
      <td>false</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

#### DNSEndpoint.spec.endpoints[index]

[↩ Parent](#dnsendpointspec)

Endpoint is a high-level way of a connection between a service and an IP

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Name</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th><th>Required</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td><b>dnsName</b></td>
      <td>string</td>
      <td>
        DNSName is the hostname of the DNS record. It is at most 253 characters, or 254
written as an absolute name with a trailing dot.
        <br/><i>Validation</i>: <code>self.size() &lt;= (self.endsWith(&#39;.&#39;) ? 254 : 253)</code>
        <br/><i>Message</i>: dnsName must be at most 253 characters, or 254 including the trailing dot
        <br/><i>Pattern</i>: <code>^(\*\.)?([a-zA-Z0-9_]([-a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9_])?\.)*[a-zA-Z0-9_]([-a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9_])?\.?$</code>
        <br/><i>Min length</i>: 1
        <br/><i>Max length</i>: 254
      </td>
      <td>true</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><b>recordType</b></td>
      <td>enum</td>
      <td>
        RecordType is the DNS record type.
        <br/><i>Enum</i>: A, AAAA, CNAME, DNAME, MX, NAPTR, NS, PTR, SRV, TLSA, TXT
      </td>
      <td>true</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><b>labels</b></td>
      <td>map[string]string</td>
      <td>
        Labels stores labels defined for the Endpoint
      </td>
      <td>false</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><b><a href="#dnsendpointspecendpointsindexproviderspecificindex">providerSpecific</a></b></td>
      <td>[]object</td>
      <td>
        ProviderSpecific stores provider specific config
        <br/><i>Max items</i>: 100
      </td>
      <td>false</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><b>recordTTL</b></td>
      <td>integer</td>
      <td>
        RecordTTL is the TTL of the record in seconds. 0 means &#34;not set&#34; and lets
the provider apply its own default. The upper bound is the RFC 2181 §8 maximum.
        <br/><i>Format</i>: int64
        <br/><i>Minimum</i>: 0
        <br/><i>Maximum</i>: 2147483647
      </td>
      <td>false</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><b>setIdentifier</b></td>
      <td>string</td>
      <td>
        SetIdentifier distinguishes multiple records with the same name and type
(e.g. Route53 records with routing policies other than &#39;simple&#39;).
        <br/><i>Max length</i>: 255
      </td>
      <td>false</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><b>targets</b></td>
      <td>[]string</td>
      <td>
        Targets are the values the DNS record points to. Leaving it empty is only
